newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah volatile on band and politics.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah volatile on band and politics.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah was volatile against the dollar in moderate trading at midday on Wednesday, dealers said.

They said the rupiah strengthened at mid-morning following a report in a local daily quoting a university professor and an unnamed official as saying the central bank was planning a band widening in the near future.
Spot rupiah rose to a high of 2,417.5 from an opening of 2,418.5/19.5 on the back of the report, but was later ignored by the market as operators switched focus to politics.
A noted economist said the central bank was unlikely to widen its band in the short- or medium-term because there was no fundamental reason to back it up at present.
"The rate is hovering at a healthy level below the mid-rate of the intervention band and moderately higher than the floor rate. I don't see any reason to act now," the economist said.
He said the central bank had implemented a new reserve rate of five percent only last week which should help contain money supply growth, which exceeded the government target in 1996.
The economist said there was no immediate reason to act and the effect of the new reserve rate had to be digested first.
Meanwhile, operators switched focus to political issues as the campaign for general elections on May 29 will start Sunday.
One currency dealer in Singapore said the tone had turned biddish for the dollar after the lunch-break.
"Political issues are taking the lead for now. People are worried over possible riots and things like that as we enter the campaign period," the dealer said.
Spot rupiah weakened to 2,420.0/21.0 at 0545 GMT.
One local bank dealer said there could be more upside for the dollar after it broke the resistance level of 2,420.0.
Bank Indonesia raised its intervention band by one point to 2,403/2,595 and the conversion band at 2,403/2,451 on Tuesday.
